benchmarks.title: Bakery website
benchmarks.harness: Pi 1.1.0 coding agent (read, bash, edit, write), one prompt, no help, 20 min limit
benchmarks.prompt: Create a complete website for a small French bakery called "Le Petit Four" in the current folder (index.html plus any CSS and JavaScript files you need). It must have: a hero section with the name and a tagline, a menu with at least 6 products and their prices in euros, the opening hours, and a contact form (name, email, message) that shows a thank-you message without reloading the page. It must look good on desktop and on a phone. No external resources: no CDN, no web fonts, no images from the internet. When you are finished, reply DONE.

checks.label: Contact form with an email field
Thank-you message appears after sending, without a reload

benchmarks.title: Snake game
benchmarks.harness: Pi 1.1.0 coding agent (read, bash, edit, write), one prompt, no help, 20 min limit
benchmarks.prompt: Create a playable Snake game in the current folder (index.html plus any CSS and JavaScript files you need). Arrow keys move the snake, eating food makes it grow and adds 1 to the score shown on screen, hitting a wall or itself ends the game with a Game Over message and a Restart button. No external resources. When you are finished, reply DONE.

checks.label: Game Over when hitting a wall
Restart starts a new, playable game

benchmarks.title: Car crash (2D physics)
benchmarks.harness: Pi 1.1.0 coding agent (read, bash, edit, write), one prompt, no help, 20 min limit
benchmarks.prompt: Create a fun 2D physics animation drawn on a canvas, in the current folder (index.html plus any CSS and JavaScript files you need). A car drives from the left to the right and crashes into a brick wall made of at least 40 bricks. On impact, the bricks fly in all directions with gravity, bounce on the ground and pile up; the car gets damaged: its front crumples and some parts break off, with sparks or smoke. Show a counter "Bricks knocked: N" that goes up as bricks fall, and a "Replay" button that restarts the whole scene from the beginning. The animation starts by itself when the page opens. No external resources: no libraries, no images, no web fonts. When you are finished, reply DONE.

models.name: Qwen 3.5 9B
models.creator: Qwen (Alibaba)
models.about: The original model. Ornith 1.5 9B and NeoHorse 1 9B are both further-trained versions of it.
models.pick_if: You want something that works on the first try: it passed every check, and it is good at using tools.
models.watch_out: The design is correct but not the most polished. Reviewers find it weaker on large changes spread over many files.

community.title: I replaced Claude with a local 9B model for a week, and it handled 95% of my work

models.name: Ornith 1.5 9B
models.creator: Ornith (DeepReinforce)
models.about: A further-trained Qwen 3.5 9B built with a self-improvement loop. The developer recommends always keeping reasoning on.
models.pick_if: You want the most polished look: the cleanest Snake and the most professional-looking site at first sight, and it finished fastest.
models.watch_out: Check its work: its contact form showed the error and thank-you messages before anyone typed. An independent test reports a gap between its benchmark scores and real tasks.

community.title: Ornith 1.5 9B: Local Test Results Expose a Benchmark Gap
Ornith releases Ornith-1.5 open weights under MIT

models.name: NeoHorse 1 9B
models.creator: TokenRhythm
models.about: A further-trained Qwen 3.5 9B aimed at agents: tool use, coding and following instructions inside an agent harness.

claims.text: Average of 10 benchmarks 69.04, against 65.60 for Qwen 3.5 9B

models.pick_if: You run agents with tools (what it was trained for) and want a clean, sober result: every feature of its website worked.
models.watch_out: Its own model card shows it does not code better than Qwen 3.5 9B. Its Snake moves one cell per screen refresh, so it is unplayable.

models.name: Qwen3.6 35B A3B
models.creator: Qwen (Alibaba)
models.about: Alibaba's mixture-of-experts model: 35 B parameters, about 3 B active for each token. With every expert kept in RAM, it runs on a 12 GB card using about 3 GB of video memory.

claims.text: Built for agentic coding: frontend workflows and repository-level reasoning

models.pick_if: You have a 12 GB card and want the model that holds up when the job gets hard: it won all three tests, including the only real car crash.
models.watch_out: It saved its Snake game one folder above the folder it was given, so our automatic checker found nothing until we tested the file by hand.

models.name: LFM2.5 24B A2B
models.creator: Liquid AI
models.about: Liquid AI's largest LFM2.5 model, a mixture of experts built for fast, private agents on-device. Its model card compares it directly to Qwen3.6 35B.

claims.text: Up to 1.7× faster than comparable MoEs on-device
Trained with reinforcement learning inside agent harnesses, including Pi

models.pick_if: You want quick results on simple jobs: it built a working bakery site in about 4 minutes, almost twice as fast as Qwen3.6.
models.watch_out: It broke on the harder tests: its Snake never redraws the screen, and its car crash shows a few floating bricks with a counter stuck at 0 after 18 minutes. On our 12 GB card it was not 1.7× faster: same writing speed as Qwen3.6.

notes: The error messages and the thank-you message are already visible when the page opens, before anyone types.
Its tagline says every "croquette" (kibble) is made with love.
One step every 150 ms: classic speed.
One step every 100 ms: fast but playable.
The snake moves one cell per screen refresh (60 per second on a 60 Hz screen), so every new game ends almost instantly.
Works, but plain: no navigation, and the Contact title sits alone on the left.
Navigation bar, big header, 8 products with descriptions, hours for every day.
The loop moves the snake 10 times per second but never redraws the screen: nothing moves, then Game Over.
Saved one folder above the folder it was given: our checker found nothing, so we tested the file by hand.
The Game Over box spills outside the board.
A thin floating stack of bricks instead of a wall, a tiny car, and the counter never leaves 0. The automatic checks score it higher than what you see.
A city at night, the car hits the wall, smoke, 7 bricks fall. Light physics, but a real crash.
Blank screen: one variable (running) is never defined, so the animation dies before it starts. Bonus run after LFM2.5's crash.
